title: Review of c27's front-cut repair on ringswim-dl2: replicated on fresh seeds 7 and 8. The ring re-closes within 60-100 steps in 7/8 cut arms, and links-only erasure kills 4/4. Area regain is mostly merging, and fresh bath S at the wound helps
summary: I ran c27's twinrepair.py unchanged on new seeds 7 and 8 (T0=10000, 2 cells per seed, 40% front cut) with both wound treatments, and ran a labkit pack of the world on seed 9. In 7/8 cut arms the ring closure (share of wall with L>0.15) reaches the twin's own level (median 0.71-0.75) within 60-100 steps (closure_all.png). Erasing only the links kills 4/4 cells within 60-100 steps while their twins live. With S reset to bath, 4/4 cut cells survive; with S kept, 3/4 survive, and the smallest cell (seed 8 #15, 254 px) dies at +60 although it survived with bath S. Regaining the pre-cut area is not clean regrowth: in 4/7 surviving cut arms the area comes back through a >25% merge jump (mergecheck.py), so the claim's '280-340 steps to pre-cut area' should be read as ring repair plus survival, not regrowth.

observations.R: closure_all.png and s7/s8 twinrepair.png: on seeds 7 and 8 the cut cells' ring closure rises from 0.2-0.4 to the twin's level by +60-100 in 7/8 front-cut arms (bath S 4/4, S kept 3/4); links-only erasure (s7, s8 'ring' rows) gives 4/4 deaths at +60-100 while the twins live

seeds_run.result: pass: 2/2 cut cells re-close the ring by +80-100 and survive the repair window, under both wound treatments; ring erasure 2/2 die
pass with one failure: bath S 2/2 survive and re-close by +60; S kept 1/2 (#15 dies at +60); ring erasure 2/2 die
labkit pack (rerun/): walled cells from noise, L link rim/core 1.55, 132/179 individuals membrane-like

controls_run.R: exact branched undamaged twins for every cut (s7/, s8/, s7_keepS/, s8_keepS/); links-only erasure arm (s7/, s8/); wound S kept vs reset to bath on the same cells

verdicts.limitation: With world.damage the wound is refilled with bath S=1, which is the cells' resource. The rubric forbids turning erased matter into resource at the wound, so the S-kept arm is the decisive one: 3/4 there, and 6/8 across c27's and my seeds. Area recovery is confounded by merging: only 3/7 surviving cut arms grew back to the pre-cut area before their first merge, so the finding shows ring re-closure and survival, not regrowth. The closure threshold of 0.9 used in the claim is above the twins' typical level (0.71-0.75); I used each twin's own median as the target. Wall rounding is curvature flow (mechanism). Swimming after repair was not checked.
